value.rationale: The newly proved shape-uniform second-order approach law answers a natural quantitative question at a convex-geometric limiting construction. Its first coefficient is a sharp, dimension-dependent chord entropy observable, and its second records genuine logarithmic variance. The dimension-only remainder holds over all K without shape regularity, transfers to volume, and yields a strictly positive first-order volume deficit and quantitative cylinder stability. These data give a reusable benchmark beyond the existing qualitative limit, though the finite-parameter inequality itself is known.
